plan.title: docs(agents): AGENTS.md wrongly says scope provenance is warn-only, and every agent reads it

narratives.Description: docs(agents): AGENTS.md wrongly says scope provenance is warn-only, and every agent reads it
narratives.Overview:
> **Recut after an N=3 design-critique panel.** The original filing claimed `verify:scope-provenance` was fail-closed but unenforced. That was false and is withdrawn — see the correction at [5404959945](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3712#issuecomment-5404959945), the successor lean at [5404981746](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3712#issuecomment-5404981746), and the accepted synthesis with verified-claims table at [5405122964](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3712#issuecomment-5405122964). Two findings that outgrew this issue were spun out; this one keeps the single wrong sentence.

## Problem

`AGENTS.md:287` tells every agent in this repository that scope provenance is warn-only. It is not.

```
! Test placement + scope provenance (#3145) - `deft verify:test-boundary`,
  `deft verify:scope-provenance`, `deft verify:consumer-check-contract`
  (docs: ...); defaults warn-only until authored policy.
```

`--enforce` governs only the **empty-scope** case. A brief that declares a non-empty `file_scope` without a base-committed approval fails closed with or without it. That is the failure operators actually hit, and the pinned rule says it cannot happen.

## Why this matters more than a typo

The sentence sits in the always-applied block that every agent session reads before doing anything. An agent that has read it will:

- treat a `verify:scope-provenance` failure as advisory and route around it
- advise an operator that a same-change-set approval is safe to ship
- not budget for the two-PR approval shape, because it does not believe the gate can block

All three happened in this session. The chain ran: read the line, believed the gate was advisory, told the operator to ship the deviation, watched the required merge gate go red on PR #3711. The false sentence was the first link.

## Evidence that it is enforced

- `Taskfile.yml:435` — `verify:scope-provenance` is a `deps:` entry of `check:framework-source`
- `Taskfile.yml:411-416` — `check:merge` is an alias calling `check:framework-source`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:119` and `:388` — `run: task check:merge`
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml:59` — the `merge-gate` aggregator is required
- PR #3711 merge gate, observed red:

```
Failed to run task "check:merge" -> "check:framework-source"
  -> "verify:scope-provenance": exit status 1
verify_scope_provenance: 1 self-authorization violation(s) (#3145).
```

## Scope

Correct the sentence. Say what `--enforce` actually governs, and that a declared `file_scope` without base approval fails closed regardless.

Check whether the same claim is repeated elsewhere — `content/templates/agents-entry.md` mirrors consumer-relevant maintainer rules under the #1309 propagation discipline, so a fix here likely needs `task agents:refresh`.

The two `deft verify:*` verbs named alongside it in the same clause, `verify:test-boundary` and `verify:consumer-check-contract`, may genuinely be warn-only. Confirm each independently rather than assuming the clause is uniformly right or uniformly wrong. `verify_test_boundary` prints `WARN ... (migration/discovery mode; not failing)` in CI logs, which suggests the clause is a true statement about some of its subjects and a false one about scope provenance.

## Out of scope

Spun out of this issue after the panel:

- surfacing the approval obligation at activation instead of at a red gate
- the empty-fence ratio: 600 plan ids declare a `file_scope`, 4 approval records exist

## Acceptance

- [ ] `AGENTS.md:287` no longer claims scope provenance defaults warn-only
- [ ] The corrected text states what `--enforce` governs (the empty-scope case) and that a declared non-empty `file_scope` without base approval fails closed
- [ ] Each other verb named in that clause is checked and described accurately
- [ ] `content/templates/agents-entry.md` propagation handled if the rule is consumer-relevant (#1309), with `task agents:refresh` run
- [ ] No gate, verifier, or policy default is changed — this is a documentation correction only (#3156)
- [ ] CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` entry

Refs #3145, #3205, #3385.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-25T04:00:25Z)

model: claude-opus-5-thinking-high-fast
role: triage

**mechanism-shaped: true**

design-critique: warranted, because the issue asks which mechanism should hold a fail-closed gate that nothing invokes, and every available answer changes behaviour for every story PR in the repo. "Wire it into CI" and "call it advisory" are not variations on one design — they are different products with different costs. The mint verb's missing in-flight path is a second, separable mechanism question layered on the first. Neither is settled by the issue body.

## Authorship disclosure

I authored #3712 and I am running this arc as parent. Under Non-self-arbitration (design-critique contract, Stop 5), any finding I originated must satisfy Decorrelation — primary-source re-derivation or a cross-family re-check — before it can appear as verified. Critic agreement with my framing does not verify it. The findings most exposed to this are the two I measured myself, and both should be independently re-derived rather than taken from me:

- that `verify:scope-provenance` appears in no workflow under `.github/workflows/`
- that `.deft/**` is absent from any path-aware cheap CI lane

## Triage decision

Accepted. `d9801c94-96e7-4617-b578-0dda98e641e4`.

## Variant (Stop 2)

**panel, N=3.** No defensible presumption is on offer, the solution space is genuinely open, and blast radius is high. Enforcing this gate would put a new fail-closed check in front of every story PR at a moment when the repo is actively cutting CI cost (#3678); declaring it advisory retires a protection the framework advertises. Those are opposite directions and the issue body picks neither. N=1 would return one opinion on a fork that needs disagreement to be useful.

## What the panel is being asked to judge

Two separable mechanisms, and critics should feel free to conclude they need separate dispositions:

1. **Enforcement posture.** `verify:scope-provenance` is written fail-closed and is invoked by nothing. Either wire it in, or change the framing to match reality. Same class as #3703 (`verify:routing`, fail-closed and uninvoked), which suggests a pattern worth naming rather than two one-off fixes.
2. **Mint ergonomics.** `scope:record-approved-scope` instructs the operator to commit the approval on the merge base, and offers no supported way to do that once a PR is open.

## Known-state disclosure

This arc's own trigger case is unresolved on PR #3711 (#3708). The operator minted approval for a corrected seven-path `file_scope`, the verifier reported `self-authorizing-scope-expansion`, and the operator elected to ship with the deviation recorded rather than land a corrective pre-PR. That decision is made and is not the panel's to relitigate. It is stated here because it is evidence about what the current mechanism costs in practice, and because a critic reading the thread will find it.

## Release constraint

The operator wants this in the imminent release. That constrains the buildable scope, not the critique. If the panel concludes the honest fix is larger than the release window, say so — a correct "this does not fit" is more useful than a scoped-down answer that leaves the gate in its current state.


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-25T04:05:14Z)

model: gpt-5.6-sol-medium
role: critic

### Blocking — The “unenforced” premise is false

At dispatch SHA `8bb1e5282f18367c75e868b44898791f5acfa8bb`, the workflow has no literal `verify:scope-provenance` step, but it runs on every pull request without a path filter and executes `task check:merge` (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:3-6`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:83-119`). That target delegates to `check:framework-source`, whose dependency list includes `verify:scope-provenance` (`Taskfile.yml:411-440`). Root `task check` also resolves the framework checkout to that same aggregate (`Taskfile.yml:395-404`, `packages/core/src/check/context.ts:47-51`). Therefore “nothing runs automatically” and “absent from workflow text means absent from CI” are both incorrect.

The posture is nuanced, but not advisory in the trigger case. The CLI defaults `enforce` to false (`packages/cli/src/verify-scope-provenance.ts:17-33`), yet a same-change-set record/preimage rewrite is unconditionally added as a hard finding (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts:693-710`), and a modified active brief with non-empty unapproved scope is also hard-failed regardless of `--enforce` (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts:391-409`, `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts:765-777`). Only the empty-scope missing-digest migration case is warn-only by default (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts:765-803`). Wiring a second CI invocation would duplicate the gate; adding `--enforce` would chiefly change that migration case, not repair the reported seven-path violation.

This is not the same wiring class as `verify:routing`. Routing is defined as a standalone task (`tasks/verify.yml:188-197`) but is absent from both framework and consumer check gate lists, while scope provenance is present in both (`packages/core/src/check/gate-lists.ts:100-104`, `packages/core/src/check/gate-lists.ts:127-140`). The broader pattern is instead “do not infer reachability from literal workflow text; trace aggregate targets.”

### Blocking — A direct merge-base mint would violate the current authority model

The issue is correct that `scope:record-approved-scope` has no merge-base, prior-PR, target-ref, or alternate-worktree output mode. Its public arguments are path/actor/kind/project-root/path binding/repo/quiet (`packages/cli/src/scope-record-approved-scope.ts:121-190`), and production mint writes the pair under the supplied project root (`packages/cli/src/scope-record-approved-scope.ts:276-306`, `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/mint-artifacts.ts:503-535`). The evaluator’s `renewedApprovals` map is explicitly a test seam, not an operator channel (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts:60-77`); the verify CLI passes only base ref and enforce state (`packages/cli/src/verify-scope-provenance.ts:58-68`). So the in-flight direct-mint capability is genuinely unsupported, not merely undocumented.

But unsupported does not make the ordering accidental. The documented contract requires the record and preimage to be committed on the merge base before activation/expansion (`content/docs/scope-provenance.md:59-67`, `content/docs/scope-provenance.md:93-103`), and explicitly defines first adoption and expansion as two-PR flows (`content/docs/scope-provenance.md:126-142`). The evaluator reads authority with `git show <base>:` and rejects a branch-local rewrite (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts:319-357`, `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts:650-710`). #3205 recorded “separately committed expanded human approval on base” as acceptance, and #3385 strengthened that to a base-committed record plus preimage (`xbrief/completed/2026-08-08-3205-scope-provenance-first-adoption-and-base-approval.xbrief.json:33-44`, `xbrief/completed/2026-08-16-3385-verifyscope-provenance-must-pin-extracted-intent-preimage-au.xbrief.json:35-52`).

A command cannot retroactively put an artifact into an existing merge-base commit. It could prepare an approval-only branch/PR or write into a separately checked-out base worktree, but merging that approval is still the independent authorization event. A “mint directly against merge base” that lets the implementation PR consume an unmerged/local artifact would collapse the anti-self-authorization boundary the verifier is designed to enforce. Preserve the antecedent approval; improve how the approval-only change is prepared and reviewed.

### Sharpening — The actual defect is lifecycle discovery and transaction cost

The code and docs agree on the two-step model, but the normal activation surface does not expose it. `scope:activate` only invokes the lifecycle transition (`tasks/scope.yml:51-59`), while the mint task separately says “Commit on merge base before activation/expansion PR” (`tasks/scope.yml:160-174`). That mismatch explains late discovery more directly than missing CI wiring: CI catches the violation, but only after the operator has already activated and implemented.

The lean should therefore separate two choices:

1. Add a pre-activation/pre-implementation readiness check that detects non-empty `file_scope` without a base-visible record + preimage and prints the approval-only next step. This makes the existing security model usable without weakening it.
2. Reduce approval-only change cost. There is no `.deft/**` path-filtered lane; the only workflow-level `paths:` filter is docs-site-only (`.github/workflows/docs-site.yml:9-15`), while the main CI is unfiltered and runs the full merge gate (`.github/workflows/ci.yml:3-6`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:83-119`). A cheap approval lane may improve feedback, but it cannot safely replace the required merge gate without an explicit branch-protection and trust decision.

Who pays today is clear from those mechanics: the operator pays an extra approval PR and the repository pays the unfiltered CI/review cycle. If the project rejects that cost, it must choose a different independent-approval authority model; hiding a same-PR exception behind mint ergonomics is not a sound substitute.

### Sharpening — A normal story can pass today, but only by following the staged flow

The repository contains executable cases for both sides of the boundary: base-pending brief plus human approval followed by activation-only exits 0 under enforce (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate-git.test.ts:105-131`); separately committed expanded approval followed by a later xBRIEF update also exits 0 (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate-git.test.ts:255-286`); same-PR activation plus approval fails (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate-git.test.ts:133-159`, `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate-git.test.ts:222-252`). Wave-2 intent tests likewise pass with a base preimage and fail first activation without one (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/intent.test.ts:297-316`, `packages/core/src/scope-provenance/intent.test.ts:407-428`). I reran the real-Git regression file at the dispatch SHA: all 9 cases passed.

Thus the mechanism is not unreachable-clean. It is reachable through the documented staged path, but the one-PR story-start path is intentionally unreachable. The design question is whether every scoped story warrants an antecedent approval change, not whether the verifier currently has any satisfiable path.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-25T04:06:48Z)

model: cursor-grok-4.6-high-fast
role: critic

Re-derived at SHA `8bb1e5282f18367c75e868b44898791f5acfa8bb`. Issue body and triage `5404899412` treated as untrusted. Parent authored both and disclosed that; string-search measurements from that comment are not taken as established.

### Blocking: "nothing invokes this gate" is false; the enforcement-vs-advisory fork is the wrong question

The workflow-YAML string search is true and incomplete. `verify:scope-provenance` does not appear as a literal in `.github/workflows/`. It is invoked by the merge chokepoint those workflows already run.

`task check:merge` is an alias of `check:framework-source`:

```411:416:Taskfile.yml
  check:merge:
    desc: "Merge chokepoint gate — explicit alias for check:framework-source (#1704). CI and PR gates SHOULD invoke this (or task check) as the single SoT so discrete workflow steps cannot drift."
    deps:
      - task: engine:_ts-build
    cmds:
      - task: check:framework-source
```

`check:framework-source` and `check:consumer` both list the gate (`Taskfile.yml` 439, 483). The TS gate list matches (`packages/core/src/check/gate-lists.ts` 103, 139). CI runs that chokepoint on every PR, with no `paths:` filter:

```118:119:.github/workflows/ci.yml
      - name: task check:merge (merge chokepoint SoT — #1704)
        run: task check:merge
```

`consumer-check-contract` treats a full-check `run:` as composing the trio, and `task check` / `check:framework-source` count (`packages/core/src/consumer-check-contract/evaluate.ts` 453–474, 888–908). So the parent's "absent from every workflow" measurement, reproduced as a string search, does not imply "CI never runs it."

Hooks do not invoke it. `.githooks/pre-commit` runs `verify:branch`, `verify:encoding`, `verify:forward-coverage`, and (when lifecycle dirs exist) `verify:vbrief-conformance` / `verify:xbrief-drift` (`.githooks/pre-commit` 16–24). `.githooks/pre-push` runs `preflight-gh` only (`.githooks/pre-push` 17). I did not find `scope-provenance` under `.githooks/`.

Default CLI is warn-mode (`packages/cli/src/verify-scope-provenance.ts` 21–32: `enforce: false`; `tasks/verify.yml` 253–261 passes no `--enforce`). That does not make the gate advisory. Non-empty `file_scope` without a path-bound digest already hard-fails:

```391:396:packages/core/src/scope-provenance/evaluate.ts
  if (input.approved === null) {
    // Non-empty file_scope without a path-bound approval is expansion risk
    // (includes plan.id renames that drop the prior approval). Hard-fail so the
    // default check path cannot soft-warn past AC "fails until renewed approval".
    // Empty-scope body-only edits may still soft-warn under migration (no enforce).
    const hard = input.enforce || currentScope.length > 0;
```

Same-PR approval rewrite is also always a hard finding (`evaluate.ts` 693–709, 776–777). Soft-warn is only the empty-scope missing-digest migration path (`evaluate.ts` 765–773, 790–802).

Disposition cost: relabeling the verb "advisory" would deny a check that already fails `task check` / merge-gate when an active brief with non-empty `file_scope` is in the change set. "Wire it into CI" is already done. Neither fork in the issue body is the remaining design.

### Blocking: #3703 is not the same class

#3703 (`verify:routing`) claims no Taskfile target, no hook, no workflow. This gate is on the `task check` / `check:merge` path above. A fail-closed pre-dispatch verb with no caller, and a merge-gate member whose documented pass requires a prior master-landed approval, are different products. Folding them into one "wire it or call it advisory" pattern will pick the wrong repair for at least one of them.

I did not re-derive #3703's Taskfile/hook/workflow counts; I used that issue only as a contrast the parent named.

### Blocking: the approval-ordering model is the load-bearing defect, not an unwired verifier

#3205 and #3385 asked for this shape, and the code matches.

#3205 completed brief: authority is the merge-base record; pending→active passes only when that record already authorizes current scope; same-change-set rewrite hard-fails; expansion passes only after a separately committed base approval (`xbrief/completed/2026-08-08-3205-scope-provenance-first-adoption-and-base-approval.xbrief.json` items at lines 19–38).

#3385 completed brief: "First activation with nonempty scope requires a base-committed pin. Same-PR rewrite fails" (`xbrief/completed/2026-08-16-3385-verifyscope-provenance-must-pin-extracted-intent-preimage-au.xbrief.json` lines 38, 120). Docs repeat the same sequence (`content/docs/scope-provenance.md` 126–142, 59–61, 93).

"Same change set" is the whole PR, not one commit. Discovery is `git diff <base>...HEAD` plus working tree (`evaluate.ts` 208–228). A first-commit mint and a second-commit activate on the same branch both appear in `origin/master...HEAD`. That is why remediation says "merge base (or a prior PR)" (`evaluate.ts` 278–286, 705–708) and why `mint-artifacts.ts` cannot fix it by writing a better file in the current tree.

A normal one-PR activate+implement story with non-empty `file_scope` therefore cannot pass, by design. A practiced implement PR that never touches `xbrief/active/` can pass vacuously: `evaluateOneScopeProvenance` returns null when the active brief is not in the change set (`evaluate.ts` 381–384), and the evaluator only lists `xbrief/active/` (`evaluate.ts` 270–276). On this SHA, recent product commits such as `87c73c78` (#3658) and `f638764e` (#3654) carry no xBRIEF path; leftover completed-tracked artifacts land later. #3637 did the documented two-step: `011e8cee` landed only `.deft/approved-scope/issue-3637-*`, then `188f3b23` implemented without rewriting those files.

So: if the gate is "enforced today," the common story that omits the active brief from the PR is green; the story that presents the brief the gate was written to police is red unless a prior approval PR already merged. That is not a missing invocation. It is a model that is internally consistent and incompatible with the one-PR story flow this repo actually ships.

Who pays for each remaining choice:

- Keep merge-base-first, surface it at `scope:activate`, document `git add -f` in this repo. Operators pay a pre-implementation PR on every non-empty `file_scope` story. CI and paid review pay for that extra PR (see sharpening on lanes). The self-auth property stays.
- Relabel advisory / stop hard-failing. Nobody pays at merge time. The rare PR that does carry an active brief can self-authorize again. That walks #3205/#3385 back.
- Change the ordering model (same-branch sequential commits, or a TTY mint that is not "same change set" as the brief). Design cost now; operators stop hitting a dead remediation. The security property must be restated: human-presence mint, not "approval already on master."

I would not wire a second invocation point, and I would not call the current verb advisory. I would treat the ordering requirement as the thing under design, because that is what makes the documented remediation unreachable from an open implementation PR.

### Sharpening: mint has no merge-base writer; "no path once a PR is open" overstates

`mintApprovedScopeArtifacts` writes record + preimage into the current working tree under `.deft/approved-scope/` (`packages/core/src/scope-provenance/mint-artifacts.ts` 503–535). `MintArtifactsInput` has no `baseRef`, onto-ref, checkout, or commit field (74–99). CLI flags are path, `--actor`, `--confirm`, `--kind`, `--project-root`, `--xbrief-rel-path`, `--repo`, `--quiet` (`packages/cli/src/scope-record-approved-scope.ts` 64–71, 121–169). After a successful mint it only prints "commit record + preimage on the merge base (or a prior PR)" (322–324). `tasks/scope.yml` 166–174 is the same wrap.

Merge-base mint is genuinely unimplemented, not merely undocumented. That is not the same as "no supported operator path." The supported path is a second PR that lands the two JSON files on master, then rebase the implementation branch so the approval is no longer in `base...HEAD`. This repo has already done that (`011e8cee`). The issue lists that path as a bad option (full stack + paid review), not as a missing verb. Cost is real; "unsupported" is not.

`scope:activate` does not mention mint, digest, or provenance. I grepped `packages/core/src/vbrief-activate/` and `packages/cli/src/vbrief-activate.ts`: no `approved-scope` / `record-approved-scope` / `scope-provenance` hits. The obligation lives in docs and in failure text, which matches the issue's "why this recurs" on surfacing, not on invocation.

### Sharpening: in this repo the authority store is gitignored; consumers are different

```56:56:.gitignore
.deft/
```

`git check-ignore -v .deft/approved-scope/example.json` → `.gitignore:56:.deft/`. There is no `!.deft/approved-scope/` exception. New mints will not appear in `git add` without `-f`. Docs and remediation never say `-f`.

Six records are already tracked (force-add precedent): `3291-decompose-structural-grant-cli.json`, `issue-3438-shell-dest-form-scope-gate.{json,intent.json}`, `issue-3637-doctor-header-drift-bare-vbrief.{json,intent.json}`, `story-3124-scm-label-mirror-operator-discovery.json`. So the intended store is versioned, and the ignore rule fights that store in this repository.

Consumer `CANONICAL_GITIGNORE_BASELINE` is selective (`.deft/cache/`, `.deft/routing.local.json`, …) and does not blanket-ignore `.deft/` or `.deft/approved-scope/` (`packages/core/src/init-deposit/gitignore.ts` 34–41). I did not verify every consumer clone; the deposited baseline is the consumer contract I could read. A "corrective PR of two JSON files" is a this-repo ignore + this-repo CI-cost problem, not automatically a consumer-mechanism problem.

`.deft/**` is not on any path-filtered cheap lane. The only `paths:` filter under `.github/workflows/` is `docs-site.yml` 12–14 (`docs-site/**`, that workflow file). `ci.yml` and `ci-lane.yml` have no path filters. I confirmed by search, not by executing every workflow.

### Blocking 1 -- The issue's central premise is false. `verify:scope-provenance` is invoked by `task check`, runs in CI on every PR, and was the sole named cause of the red merge gate on PR #3711 at the moment #3712 was filed.

The issue states it "is a fail-closed self-authorization gate that **nothing runs automatically**" and "is absent from every workflow in `.github/workflows/`."

The literal string is absent from the workflow files. The gate is not.

```439:440:Taskfile.yml
      - verify:scope-provenance
      - verify:consumer-check-contract
```

That is a `deps:` entry of `check:framework-source` (`Taskfile.yml:418`). `check:merge` is a pure alias for it:

```411:416:Taskfile.yml
  check:merge:
    desc: "Merge chokepoint gate — explicit alias for check:framework-source (#1704). CI and PR gates SHOULD invoke this (or task check) as the single SoT so discrete workflow steps cannot drift."
    deps:
      - task: engine:_ts-build
    cmds:
      - task: check:framework-source
```

And CI runs exactly that, in both the primary and the failover merge-gate jobs:

```118:119:.github/workflows/ci.yml
      - name: task check:merge (merge chokepoint SoT — #1704)
        run: task check:merge
```

(same at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:387-388`). It is also in both typed gate lists:

```101:104:packages/core/src/check/gate-lists.ts
  // #3145: test/source boundary + approved-scope provenance + consumer gate composition
  "verify:test-boundary",
  "verify:scope-provenance",
```
